description.narrative: The proposed Expanded Social Assistance Project will build on a decade of Asian Development Bank support for social protection in the Philippines. The 2010 Social Protection Support Project helped establish the national poverty targeting system, and supported implementation and evaluation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino conditional cash transfer (CCT) program. Additional financing approved in 2016 funded a share of the CCT education and health grants for more than four million households nationwide. ADB technical assistance has strengthened capacity and delivered demand-driven policy and advisory support to inform program reforms. While the proposed third phase of support will continue to strengthen the CCT program, it will also help to build a more integrated and efficient social protection system. It will finance transfers and strengthen implementation mechanisms (including payment, financial management, and targeting) for the government's expanded social transfers, including the social pension program. The project will support the Philippine Development Plan 2017-2022 goal of helping individuals and families cope with risks through a universal and transformative social protection system that builds socioeconomic resilience.

Output: (Under TA facility) CCT delivery systems strengthened Indicator: At least 95% of monitored children 6-18 years old in 4Ps households are assigned a DepEd Learner Reference Number in the PPIS (2019 baseline: 58%) Achievement: 91.68 Progress/Status: As of 30 June 2024:
Overall Average: 91.68% (7,050,412 out of 7,690,390 - 2019-2022 cumulative total)
Source: National CV Turnout from P2 2024
Actions Taken:
The EA conducted massive updating, capturing of the LRN of children enrolled in school in October 2023. It also directed the DSWD field offices to capture the LRN of children 6-14 years old as part of the massive updating instruction dated 6 July 2023. DSWD also coordinated with DepEd for strategies on capturing LRN.
On 8 November 2023, the DepEd issued a Memorandum Order requesting the SDOs to assist the 4Ps workers in providing the LRN of 4Ps children until December 2023. Simultaneously, the 4Ps NPMO endorsed a memorandum to the Field Offices informing this development and requesting them to distribute the list of 4Ps children with no LRN yet to the SDOs within their jurisdiction, for the latter's assistance in providing the LRN of 4Ps children.
Catch-up Plan: 1. Fast-track finalization of the DepEd and DSWD Data Sharing Agreement; and 2. Inclusion of the capturing of LRN of 4Ps children in the 4Ps RPMO scorecard Data Source: National Program Management Office's monitoring reports

Output: (Under TA facility) Awareness building, connections with complementary social programs, project management, and evaluation capacity strengthened Indicator: DSWD-led graduation approach launched in three sites by 2022 (2019 baseline: None) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed as of 28 February 2023.
Culmination Stage. The “Padayon, SLP” Graduation Approach Pilot Project is currently on its last phase, which covers the Padayon SLP Draft Report Presentation and Turnover Workshop conducted on 22-23 February 2023, together with Asian Development Bank and BRAC-Ultra Poor Graduation Initiatives.
Accomplishments: ● Presentation of the Draft Final Report of the Padayon, SLP Graduation Approach Pilot Project; and Turnover Workshop together with developmental partners. ● Project ended last January 2023 with 83.37% of the Padayon households met the Graduation criteria ● Padayon, SLP has served 2,784 4Ps household participants in three Provinces (Iloilo, Bukidnon, and Sultan Kudarat) with 135 SLP Associations established ● 6 months preparation and 21 months implementation from April 2021 until January 2023 ● Total grants released: (SLP) P42m (approx. $770,000); (4Ps) P88m ($1.6m). TA support from ADB/DFAT amounts to $1.1 million. Total of $3.5m project cost ● Strong collaboration and support received from DFAT, ADB, BRAC-UPGI, and LGUs of target regions ● DSWD provided additional grants of P10,000 to households affected of African Swine Fever in the province of Iloilo and Bukidnon
For a household to be considered as “Graduated”, it should meet at least 7 of the 11 Graduation criteria that are applicable to all households by the end of the project. 83.37% of the Padayon households met 7 of the 11 Graduation criteria that are applicable to all households. Key Results for Graduation Criteria - End of Project: ● 73% of Padayon HHs reported an increase in their monthly income compared to baseline. ● 93% of Padayon HHs have at least one member with an active financial account in the last 30 days. ● 41% of Padayon HHs that experienced financial loss sought assistance or support to recover from major financial loss due to unexpected occurrences in the last 30 days. ● 99.44% of Padayon HHs, where participants have partners and, reported making joint decisions.
Data Source: DSWD Listahanan database maintained by NHTO and PPIS reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
